full_judgment:
2. The petitioner Major General (Retd). M. Shamsul Huq along with several others are accused in a case being Matlab P.S. Case No. 2/55 dated 3.8.91 under section 409/467/468/109 of the. Penal Code, read with section 5(2) of Act 11 of 1947. 

 3. The FIR was lodged on 3.8.90, but, the name of the petitioner does not find mention there. In the charge sheet submitted on 12.5.1992, the name of the petitioner has mentioned as an accused. It is submitted that the petitioner has been made an accused i the case only to victimize him at the instance of his political rivals. 

 5. The learned .counsel submits that as the accused petitioner does not feel secure in moving from Dhaka to the Upazila Court, Matlab he has appeared before this Court with prayer for bail. The learned counsel also referred to a similar case where the petitioner was released, on hail by 'the High Court Division in Crl Misc. case No. 117 of 1992 arising out of Matlab P.S. Case No. 6(7)91 pending in the Court of Upazila Magistrate, Matlab. For the aforesaid grounds the learned Counsel for the petitioner prays for granting bail to the accused petitioner by this court with a direction to him to appear before the Upazila Magistrates Court at Matlab with a further direction to the court below to release the accused petitioner on bail. 

 6. Mr. Aminul Huq the learned Attorney General, appearing with Mr. A. F.M. Shahid, the learned. Deputy Attorney General submits that though on principle he does not dispute the jurisdiction and power of this court in considering the prayer for bail to a person appearing before this court without going to the court of first instance, but he submits that such power would be exercised very sparingly under special, circumstances. The learned Attorney General submits that this is not a fit case where such power is required to be exercised. The learned Attorney-General has drawn our attention to the fact that the accused petitioner has already appeared before the Upazila Magistrate, Matlab, twice in connection with the other case and as such the apprehension that the petitioner will be harassed if he is go to the Upazila Magistrate Court, Matlab, sounds immaginary and vague. The learned Attorney General, further submits that giving a direction to the court below for granting bail to the petitioner as prayed for, will amount to curtailing the discretionary power of the subordinate Court. 

 7. At this stage, Mr. Moudud, the learned Counsel for the accused petitioner submits that in the instant case, no formal warrant has been issued as yet by the Upazila Magistrate, Matlab, to the knowledge of the petitioner, but the police is very vigilant to secure the arrest of the accused petitioner and if the police succeeds in securing his arrest, the petitioner who is aged 65 years, will be subjected to harassment and humiliation. Though it is not a case where the prayer for bail is made on behalf of the accused petitioner exactly in anticipation of the police arrest without there being any case against him. But it is a case where prayer for bail is made in anticipation of the arrest by the police in a case pending before the Upazila Magistrate, Matlab. 

 8. Considering the attending circumstances of the case and the fact that the accused-petitioner who has appeared before this Court is an aged Retired Army officer and as a former Minister has reason to believe that he may be harassed and humiliated during his movement from Dhaka to Matlab we allow the petitioner daintier bail in anticipation of his arrest by the police with a direction to him to surrender before the Court of Upazila Magistrate, Matlab, within 10 days from the date so as to enable him to make a prayer for bail there, if so advised.
